 Mr. JVS Deora.
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 16/11/2023

This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.72/2023 registered at Police Station Khinwsar,
District Nagaur, for offences under Sections 342, 366 and 376(2)(N) IPC.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the prosecutrix who is a mature married woman,
has falsely implicated the petitioner in a criminal case.
It was urged that the FIR has been lodged without furnishing any plausible explanation for lodging the same after a delay of more than one month.

Learned counsel submitted that the prosecutrix in her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., has stated that she was forcibly abducted by the petitioner and subjected to sexual [2023:RJ-JD:39340] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-12475/2023] assault for about 2-3 days and thereafter, she was threatened by the petitioner not to disclose the incident to anyone otherwise, her obscene photographs will be circulated on social media platforms.

sentences.text: Drawing attention of the Court towards the charge-sheet, learned counsel submitted that no such obscene video or photograph has been recovered by the investigating agency and the petitioner has not even been charged for the offence under the Information and Technology Act.
Learned counsel lastly submitted that it is highly improbable that the prosecutrix who is a mature woman, would be abducted from her house and her family members will not even come to know about it.

Learned counsel submitted that as a matter of fact, the prosecutrix voluntarily eloped with the petitioner, however, on the relations between them turning strained, the prosecutrix has falsely roped the petitioner in a criminal case.
Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is in custody; investigation against him has already been completed and the trial of the case is likely to consume sufficiently long time.
On these grounds, he implored the Court to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor so also learned counsel for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.

[2023:RJ-JD:39340] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-12475/2023] Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that FIR has been lodged against the petitioner after a delay of about one month from the date on which the prosecutrix was allegedly abducted and subjected to sexual assault by the present petitioner.

This Court also prima facie finds that specific allegation has been levelled against the petitioner that by threatening the prosecutrix to circulate her obscene photographs on social media platforms, the petitioner blackmailed her,
however, no such obscene photograph has been recovered by the investigating agency.

This Court also prima facie finds that the prosecutrix is a mature married woman and had she been forcibly abducted in the midnight of 08.03.2023, she would have shouted/cried for the help and it is highly improbable that she did not seek help from anyone or shouted for help.

This Court also prima facie finds that investigation against the petitioner has already been completed and the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the petitioner influencing the prosecution witnesses or tampering with the evidence.
In view of aforesaid, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Ram Prasad @ Lichman S/o Shri Kesharam arrested in connection with F.I.R.
No.72/2023 registered at Police Station Khinwsar, District Nagaur, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, [2023:RJ-JD:39340] (4 of 4) [CRLMB-12475/2023] provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and Ram Prasad @ Lichman vs State Of Rajasthan (2023:Rj-Jd:39340) on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23529068/
2 whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 216-Tikam/-
